name: IEC Schmitt-trigger buffer (rectangular form)
summary: Rectangular buffer carrying the hysteresis mark, meaning its input switches at two different thresholds.
description: A Schmitt-trigger buffer is an IEC 1 element with the hysteresis qualifier drawn inside the box. The qualifier states that the input has two thresholds, one for a rising signal and one for a falling signal, so the output does not chatter when the input passes slowly through the switching region.

In control panels this element usually sits at the boundary between field wiring and logic, where a slow or noisy contact or sensor signal needs squaring up. Drawings sometimes place the hysteresis mark at the input line rather than at the centre; both indicate the same bi-threshold behaviour.
The symbol does not give threshold voltages or hysteresis width. Those values belong to the device datasheet and should be checked against the field signal levels.
readingNotes: Locate the hysteresis mark; it may be centred or next to an input.
Check signal levels against the device thresholds.
drawingChecklist: Draw the hysteresis mark clearly so it is not mistaken for a waveform note.
Reference the device for threshold values.
Keep the input filter components on the same sheet.
distinction: A plain 1 buffer has a single threshold; only the hysteresis mark indicates Schmitt behaviour.
